ingenuity.caption: An artist's view of Ingenuity flying above the Martian surface.
The first black-and-white image sent back by Ingenuity from the air during Flight 1.
Perseverance's Navcam watches Ingenuity climb into the Martian sky on 19 April 2021.
Mastcam-Z on Perseverance photographs Ingenuity after its fifth flight.

viking-1.caption: The first photograph taken on the surface of Mars, by Viking 1 on 20 July 1976.
Viking Lander 1's U.S. flag on the Martian surface, photographed beside the lander.
A modern Mars orbiter view of the ground near Viking Lander 1's footpad.

insight.caption: InSight's SEIS seismometer deployed on the Martian surface under its wind and thermal shield.
One of InSight's last images, showing its dust-covered solar panels in 2022.
Before-and-after views of a fresh Martian crater made by a meteoroid impact detected by InSight.

spirit.caption: An artist's view of Spirit working in the Columbia Hills inside Gusev Crater.
Spirit's self-portrait in the McMurdo Panorama, looking back across the Columbia Hills.
Spirit's wheel churns up bright silica-rich soil at a site called Gertrude Weise.

opportunity.caption: Opportunity's self-portrait at the 'Potts' rock abrasion target in 2016.
Opportunity looks across the rim of Orion Crater during its travels in 2017.
Looking downhill from Perseverance Valley, with long Martian shadows across the rim of Endeavour Crater.

sojourner.caption: A color mosaic of Sojourner beside the Pathfinder lander and the rocky terrain of Ares Vallis.
Sojourner's own view of the Pathfinder lander after rolling down the ramp.
Sojourner sits near the 'Rock Garden' during its exploration of Ares Vallis.
Three generations of NASA Mars rovers: Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity.

dawn.caption: An artist's concept of Dawn with Vesta and Ceres in the asteroid belt.
Dawn's close view of Occator Crater and its mysterious bright spots on Ceres.
Dawn approaches Vesta in this artist's concept.
Ceres's southern hemisphere in a navigation image from Dawn's low-altitude orbit.

apollo-11.caption: A television view of Armstrong and Aldrin on the Moon, seen beside the lunar module Eagle.
Buzz Aldrin stands beside the leg of the lunar module Eagle at Tranquility Base.
Earth rises over the Moon's limb, photographed from Apollo 11 in lunar orbit.
Apollo 11 lifts off from Kennedy Space Center on 16 July 1969.

apollo-15.caption: Astronaut James Irwin salutes the U.S. flag at the Apollo 15 landing site, with the Hadley-Apennine mountains behind him.
The Apollo 15 lunar module Falcon and the Lunar Roving Vehicle at Hadley Base.
Mount Hadley rises above the lunar surface, photographed during Apollo 15's first moonwalk.
Astronaut James Irwin works at the Lunar Roving Vehicle during an Apollo 15 moonwalk.
